note: Proposed Interview for the escape rooms (phase 6), for the teacher's review before new audio is recorded. One question per room, answered by all three witnesses; each witness is met at the lock in 'at' (before its reading), never after the lock that checks them; every line is one sentence; every lie keeps its proof line. 'lines' (p, s) appear only where a statement moves to a new proof line.

into-the-hollow.question: What should a stranger know about this valley?

hans-van-ripper.truth: The farm wives christened the town, on account of their men loitering at the inn whenever they went in to sell their crops.
hans-van-ripper.lie: That hollow is a full day's journey from town, and I'll tell you plainly, it's the noisiest spot in all the county.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, I may have stretched it a little.

brom-bones.truth: He doesn't keep to the Hollow; he roams the highways too, and he likes to prowl near the old meeting house.
brom-bones.lie: He's hunting for the horse he lost, and he takes his own sweet time getting home.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, you got me; I just like to see folks jump.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: Folks who arrive clear-headed don't stay that way, and within a season they're spotting ghosts too.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: Only families born in the Hollow believe those tales, and newcomers just laugh at them.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Oh, you caught that; I only wanted to see if you were listening.

the-schoolmaster.question: What should I know about the new schoolmaster?

brom-bones.truth: Any robber could slip into that little log school easily, but he'd have a terrible time escaping again.
brom-bones.lie: That beanpole is built as solid and stocky as a blacksmith, folks say, with tiny fists to match.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, fine, he's a beanpole through and through.

hans-van-ripper.truth: He moves from one family to the next every seven days, and everything he owns fits in one bundle.
hans-van-ripper.lie: He never lifts a finger for us, not one chore, and just sits by the hearth and eats.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, all right, he helped now and then.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: On the Lord's day he plants himself before the choir loft with his best voices, sure he outshines the minister.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: He has no ear for music at all and never gives lessons in it, not for any amount of coin.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Oh, you checked; he does teach music.

tales-by-the-fire.question: What is the schoolmaster like outside the classroom?

katrina-van-tassel.truth: After worship he strolls past the graves with us girls, picking us fruit and reading the stones aloud.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: The ladies around here think a teacher is nothing special, no finer than any plowboy.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Caught me; we do think a teacher is rather grand.

brom-bones.truth: He keeps an old volume about sorcery in the colonies and trusts every word of it.
brom-bones.lie: Bugs don't bother him one bit; a June bug could smack into his face and he'd just laugh.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, you're right, a bug nearly finished him off.

hans-van-ripper.truth: He scares the grandmothers silly, telling them the earth spins about and they spend part of each day upside down.
hans-van-ripper.lie: He keeps to himself when the snow comes and won't spend his nights chatting with the grandmothers.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, fine, he was at every fireside in the valley, eating apples.

the-van-tassel-farm.question: What should I know about the Van Tassels and their farm?

brom-bones.truth: She has no brothers or sisters, and her pa is about the richest man in these parts.
brom-bones.lie: The schoolmaster saw all that livestock and never once thought about supper.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, of course he thought about supper; he thinks of nothing else.

hans-van-ripper.truth: He hardly ever thinks past his own fences, but inside them all is cozy and in good order.
hans-van-ripper.lie: His place sits up on a bare, windy hilltop, miles from any water.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, it's in a snug green nook by the water.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: A huge old tree shades our house, and the clearest drinking source in the county rises right beneath it.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: Father loves showing off his money and fancy things for all the neighbors to admire.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: All right, Father isn't one for show; he just likes a full table.
katrina-van-tassel.why: Moved off the sentences about Katrina's dress (p022), under the rule against using Irving's descriptions of her figure.

a-rival-appears.question: Who wants Katrina's hand, and what are they like?

hans-van-ripper.truth: He dreamed of hauling all their belongings and a brood of little ones off to the frontier.
hans-van-ripper.lie: When he stepped through that door he was not impressed one bit.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, the place took his heart in one look.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: The young fellows who call on me glare at one another, but they all team up the moment a newcomer shows his face.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: The young men around here are all quiet and small, and not one of them is bold or loud.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: All right, I know one who is very loud indeed.

brom-bones.truth: I'm built wide and strong, with a dark mop on my head and a grin that's half joke, half swagger.
brom-bones.lie: Nobody around here listens to me in an argument; they settle it without me.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, all right, I settle every quarrel around here.

the-feud.question: What's going on between Katrina's suitors?

katrina-van-tassel.truth: When a particular steed is tethered at our gate on the Lord's day evening, the other young men just keep walking.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: Folks around here can't stand Brom, and nobody has a kind word for him.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Fine, they rather like him, even the ones he plays tricks on.

hans-van-ripper.truth: His missus says the birds in the yard need watching, but a young lady can mind herself.
hans-van-ripper.lie: Old Baltus rules that girl with an iron hand, and she can't do a thing without his say.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, he's soft as butter with her.

brom-bones.truth: I'd have gladly met him fist to fist to end it, but the sly fellow wouldn't come near me.
brom-bones.lie: I kept calling on her every week of the year, same as always, schoolmaster or no.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, all right, I stayed away a while.

the-invitation.question: What's been happening to the schoolmaster lately?

brom-bones.truth: We plugged up the flue so his music class had to flee in a cloud of soot.
brom-bones.lie: I never pulled a single trick on him; it wasn't my style.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, guilty: every trick in the book.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: I hear he fussed for ages fixing up the one set of clothes he owns, peering into a cracked mirror.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: He kept the children late that day, finishing every lesson properly.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Oh, he let them go early because he couldn't wait.

hans-van-ripper.truth: He rode off on my old animal to court the girl, dressed up as a hero from a storybook.
hans-van-ripper.lie: That beast of mine never had a spark of spirit, not even as a colt.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, he was a firecracker once.

the-ride-to-the-party.question: What did you notice as everyone headed to the party?

brom-bones.truth: His little cap perched way down near his beak, and the back of his jacket flapped clear to his mount's rump.
brom-bones.lie: Every orchard he rode past had been stripped clean, with nothing left to pick.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, the orchards were loaded; I just like a gloomy tale.

hans-van-ripper.truth: The grandfathers came in home-woven jackets, with great clumsy footwear and big shiny clasps.
hans-van-ripper.lie: Hardly a soul turned up, and the house was half empty all night.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, it was packed to the rafters.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: The boys bind their pigtails with the hide of an eel, swearing it makes them grow thicker.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: We girls all dressed in the very newest town fashions, head to toe.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Well, maybe a ribbon or two was new.

the-feast-and-the-dance.question: What happened at the Van Tassels' feast?

brom-bones.truth: I'd never be seen on a tame, gentle mount; give me a wild one any day.
brom-bones.lie: I came on a gentle old mare that any child could ride.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, gentle is the last word for Daredevil; he would throw anyone but me.
brom-bones.why: Moved off p048 (content-noted): his truth was proved by the sentence about him brooding in a corner during the dance.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: We had fried rings of dough, twisted pastries, and every sort of treat you can name.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: Father was in a sour mood all evening and barely smiled at anyone.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: All right, Father was beaming all night, happy as could be.
katrina-van-tassel.why: Moved off p048 (content-noted). Her lie then moved off p045 too, because the lock 5 witness twist already uses that line (the same claim twice); it now rests on Baltus's good humor at the feast (p046).

hans-van-ripper.truth: Baltus didn't fuss: a firm grip, a clap on the back, a hearty roar, and he told everyone to dig in.
hans-van-ripper.lie: The schoolmaster hardly touched a crumb all night.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, he ate enough for three.

ghost-stories.question: What stories did people tell at the party?

katrina-van-tassel.truth: Some neighbors from up the valley came, spinning their spooky stories as they always do.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: Ghost stories never last in a quiet old valley like ours.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: You're right, they never fade here.

hans-van-ripper.truth: Brouwer scoffed at spooks till he had to ride double with one, and got pitched into the water.
hans-van-ripper.lie: That ghost keeps clear of the old wooden crossing and is only seen up on the mountain.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, that crossing is his favorite spot.

brom-bones.truth: I dared that rider to a contest for a drink, and my brute left his mount in the dust till he burst into flame and was gone.
brom-bones.lie: I'd never joke about that rider, because he frightens me more than anything.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, I was never frightened of him; I call him a jockey to his face.

the-lonely-road.question: How did the party end, and what came after?

hans-van-ripper.truth: He told them bits from that old Puritan writer and wonders from back where he grew up.
hans-van-ripper.lie: It was a pleasant time for a ride, cheerful as could be.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, it was gloomy as a grave that night.

brom-bones.truth: He stormed off to the barn and woke that poor beast with a smack and a boot.
brom-bones.lie: Everyone stayed the night at the Van Tassels', and not a soul left till morning.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, they all rattled off home.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: Folks pass that old tree with a mix of awe and fear, half for the poor soldier and half for the stories.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: The young people went home quietly that night without a peep.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Oh, we were giggling the whole way home.

the-headless-horseman.question: What happened on the road that night?

katrina-van-tassel.truth: That's the very place the British officer was taken, by farmers hiding in the leaves.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: Boys cross that water on their own after sunset without a second thought.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: No, the boys run past it shaking.

hans-van-ripper.truth: My old horse bolted sideways into the briars instead of crossing.
hans-van-ripper.lie: He trotted straight over the planks without a moment's fuss.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, he fought that schoolmaster every step.

brom-bones.truth: A huge rider, I hear, on a dark and mighty steed.
brom-bones.lie: When the schoolmaster sped up, that other rider fell far behind.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, that rider stuck to him like a burr, or so I hear.

brom-bones.truth: Down by the creek lay the fellow's cap, and next to it a busted gourd.
brom-bones.lie: That old nag never made it back and ran off for good.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, he was munching grass at the gate by morning.

hans-van-ripper.truth: I tossed his conjuring volumes and that scribbled poem in the fire, and my young ones are done with lessons.
hans-van-ripper.lie: He left a trunk stuffed with fine suits and silver.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, it was two shirts and a half.

katrina-van-tassel.truth: Since he owed no one and had no wife, people soon stopped thinking about him, and a new teacher took over.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: At church everyone agreed he had simply run away, and no one blamed any ghost.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Oh, they all blamed the Hessian.

the-postscript.question: What happened in the years after he disappeared?

katrina-van-tassel.truth: A neighbor back from the city says the schoolmaster lives on and even sits as a judge now.
katrina-van-tassel.lie: I never married anyone from the valley; I'm still waiting for the right one.
katrina-van-tassel.caught: Oh, you know very well whom I married.

brom-bones.truth: Not long after he vanished, I walked Katrina down the aisle as my bride.
brom-bones.lie: Folks use that old crossing as easy as you please now.
brom-bones.caught: Ha, they even moved the road to stay clear of it.

hans-van-ripper.truth: The old school went to ruin, and farm lads swear they still hear him humming hymns out there at dusk.
hans-van-ripper.lie: The grandmothers laugh at that ghost talk and say he just ran off.
hans-van-ripper.caught: Hmph, they swear he was spirited away.
